title: Annotatio III §.III: Formula words speak of action or use — Paul’s ‘bread we break’ is communion of Christ’s body, not bread outside the use
pass_a_gloss: The words clearly speak of action or use: just as Paul also expressly says concerning use or Action: The bread which we break is the Communion of the Body of Christ. For that cannot be understood of Bread outside the use, but must be taken in this way; this Bread is that thing by which the Communion of the Body of Christ is exhibited to us, and thus speak the ancient writers and principal Fathers in the Church.
pass_b_english: The words clearly speak of action or use — as Paul says expressly of use or action: the bread we break is the communion of the body of Christ.

That cannot mean bread outside the use; take it this way: this bread is the thing by which communion of Christ’s body is exhibited to us — and so speak the older writers and chief Fathers in the Church.
source_text: Verba clarè loquuntur de actione seu usu: sicut & Paulus expressè de usu seu Actione inquit: Panis quem frangimus, est Communio Corporis Christi. Id enim de Pane extra usum intelligi non potest, sed hôc modo accipiendum est; hic Panis est res illa, quâ nobis Communio Corporis Christi exhibetur, & sic loquuntur veteres scriptores & Patres praecipui in Ecclesia.
